1.text: A GUIDED SELF-AUDIT WORKBOOK · BY JAIMIE K
Now it's time to put yourself back in.
For the woman in the messy middle. The one whose life has
stopped looking like her. The map. The protocol. The way back in.

2.text: BEFORE YOU START
You're not here because you forgot who you are. You're here because you built a life around the
version of you that didn't know any better yet. And now the life doesn't fit.
You did everything you were supposed to do. Built the life, played the roles, kept going, held it together.
And somewhere along the way you stopped feeling connected to the woman living it. Now it feels blah.
You're performing instead of participating.
This isn't more inner work. You've done inner work. You've read the books, sat with the feelings, grown.
That part is handled.
What hasn't been handled is the actual life. The roles. The schedule. The relationships. The work. The
way you show up and speak. Those things were built by earlier versions of you, and they sit exactly
where you built them until you go back in and move them.
That's what this workbook is. Going back in. Moving things.
How to use it.
Read Part One in one sitting. About 40 minutes. Do the diagnostic in Chapter 4. Ten minutes. Be
honest. Lying to yourself here means you finish holding a map that doesn't reflect your actual life.
Read Part Two over the next few days. Do the scan one area at a time. Half an hour each. By the end
of the week you'll have a complete Misalignment Map.
Read Part Three. Pick your first move. Do it within 48 hours. Read Part Four after you've held the move
for at least a week.
You finish this workbook when one thing in your actual life has changed. Not a reinvention. Not a new
you. One specific thing you can point to and say that's mine now.

3.text: This isn't for everyone, and I'd rather you know now than on page 20.
If you're looking for a morning routine, a manifestation practice, or the next self-improvement plan to
install, this will frustrate the hell out of you. This book removes. It doesn't add.
This is for the woman who's done renting her life from everyone else's expectations. Who's ready to
find out which parts of the life she built are actually hers.

5.text: You built a life. You didn't know much yet, so you did what every smart woman does. You watched.
You learned. You became who each season required. The good daughter. The reliable one. The wife.
The mom. The one who holds it together.
And honestly? It kind of worked. You built the life. Checked the boxes. People are proud of you.
Then something shifted. You grew. Not in the surface way. The real way. You got clearer on what you
actually think, what you actually want, how you actually want to live. You became more yourself.
But your life didn't move with you.
The life is still shaped by the version of you that didn't know any better yet. The roles are her roles. The
schedule is her schedule. The way you answer 'how are you' is the answer you learned to give. There's
a name for this gap. Identity Lag. You changed first. Your life hasn't caught up yet.
You walk through your own days and feel a small flinch. You look at your calendar and don't fully
recognize the woman it was built for. That's the misfit.
It's not in your head. It's not a confidence issue. It's not because you haven't done enough inner work.
You built a life around yourself instead of with yourself.
This is not a mindset problem. It's a structure problem. The foundation is you.

6.text: If you drew your life on a piece of paper right now. Every role. Every commitment. Your week. Your
closest people. The way you spend a Saturday. Would that drawing look like you? Don't answer fast.
Sit with it. Most women pause here. That pause is the reason you bought this.

7.text: CHAPTER 02
How the misfit
actually happened.
Nobody planned this. You didn't make a wrong turn. You did what every honest, capable,
willing-to-show-up woman does when she builds a life with no roadmap.
You absorbed.
From your mother. From your marriage. From the church, the town, the friend group, the job. From who
you had to be at 25. None of it was bad. It worked for the people who handed it to you. It worked the
way it was designed to work.
The thing nobody told you is that other people's blueprints become your foundation if you let them. You
absorb them. You build on top of them. You forget you absorbed them. Twenty years later you can't tell
which parts of your life you actually chose and which parts you inherited.
That's how the misfit happens. Not through one bad decision. Through a thousand small ones that
made sense at the time.
The other thing nobody told you is that the inner work won't fix this. You assumed it would. You thought
if you healed enough, the life would follow.
It didn't follow. Lives don't follow. A life is a structure. Structures don't change because you became
someone new internally. They change when you go in and move the pieces.
That's not a healing problem. That's a structure problem. You don't fix a structure with more journaling.
You fix it by looking at it and changing what's there.

8.text: What's one thing you do, one role you play, or one rule you live by that you've never actually
re-examined? The thing you do because someone you trusted handed it to you?

9.text: Misalignment doesn't live everywhere. It lives in specific places. We're not rebuilding your whole life.
We're finding the places that aren't you.
There are seven of them. These are the seven areas we're going to scan.
1. Roles. Who you are to everyone else. And where you went in the process.
2. Schedule. Whose life your days are actually built around. Check before you answer.
3. Home. Your space knows which version of you lives there. Look around.
4. Relationships. Some of these fit the woman you were. Not the one reading this.
5. Work. What you do all day. Yours, or inherited?
6. Body. How you show up, dress, care for yourself. And who it's actually for.
7. Voice. What you say out loud vs. what you actually think. Mind the gap.
Most of the time, misalignment is hiding in three or four of these. The other three or four are actually
fine. Your job in the next few chapters is to figure out which is which.
Before you can do that, you need a way to tell what's you and what isn't. That's Chapter 5.

13.text: Your life mostly looks like you. You probably didn't need this workbook for the whole life. The method
still applies to any structure. Your next season, your next role, the one area that still itches. Keep going
Some of your life is you. Some of it isn't. You're in the most common spot. This is the messy middle,
and the rest of this workbook is built for exactly where you are.
Most of your life was built around someone else. This isn't a judgment. It's data. There's a lot to move,

Now do this. Underneath your total, write down the three questions you scored lowest on. Those are

14.text: CHAPTER 05
Your voice vs.
the voice you learned.
Before you can map what's yours and what isn't, you need a way to tell the difference. Most women
can't, and it's not their fault. You've absorbed so many voices, rules, and roles over the years that
you've lost track of which thoughts are originally yours.
Here's the test that works. For each piece of your life, ask:
Where did this come from?
Not do I like it. Not does it feel right. Those questions are too easy to bullshit.
If you can name where it came from. Your mother, your marriage, your church, who you were at 25.
That's not necessarily wrong. But it came from outside you, and you need to actively decide whether
you'd still build it the same way without that source.
If you can't name the source, either it's actually yours, or you've absorbed it so deeply you've forgotten.
Push harder. When did you start doing it this way? Who were you around? What season were you in?
A few examples from my own life. I kept a schedule built entirely around being available to everyone. I
told myself I liked being the reliable one. The truth was I'd inherited it from the version of me that
needed to be needed. When I sat with what my week would look like without that inheritance, it looked
different.
I answered 'how are you' with 'good, busy' for years. Nothing in that answer was mine. It was the
answer that kept every conversation comfortable.
None of this makes the people who shaped you wrong. It just wasn't you.
That's the test. Not is this good. Is this mine.

15.text: Pick one piece of your life. Any piece. Ask where it came from. Don't move on until you've named the
source or sat with the fact that you can't find one.

16.text: This is where you start making a list.
Take the three questions you scored lowest on in Chapter 4. For each one, identify the specific piece of
your life it points to. The role. The commitment. The relationship. The rule. Be specific. Not 'my
schedule in general.' The actual Tuesday obligation. The actual answer you give. The actual person.
Then for each piece, fill in: when you first started doing it this way. The source it most likely came from.
What you'd do differently if it had never been handed to you. Whether it's still right for you now.
This is the receipts work. You're naming the inheritance. Not so you can be mad about it. So you can
Most women resist this because it feels like blaming their mother, or their marriage, or admitting they
didn't think for themselves. None of that's true.
You weren't weak for absorbing what you absorbed. You were becoming. That's how it works. The
problem isn't that you absorbed. The problem is that the season that required it ended years ago and
the life still operates like it didn't.
Writing it down is how it ends. You can't move what you can't see, and you can't see it until you name
Use Worksheet 2 in the back. Fill it in for all three pieces before moving on.

18.text: This is the artifact. The piece of paper you'll be holding when this workbook ends.
On one page, you fill in seven boxes. One for each area. Each box has two halves.
LEFT SIDE: What this looks like in my life right now.
RIGHT SIDE: What this would look like if it were shaped by me, not by what I absorbed.
The right side might look almost identical to the left. That's fine. It means this area is already you. The
space between the two sides, across all seven areas, is the work.
A few things before you fill it in. The right side is not your fantasy version. Not the
run-away-to-a-new-city version. It's the smallest, most honest answer to: what would I do here if no one
If you can't fill in the right side for an area, leave it blank. Chapter 10 is for that.
Don't change anything in your life yet. We're still seeing.
Do one area per sitting. Half an hour each. You'll have the full map within a week. Fill it in by hand if
you can. Typing makes this feel like a planning exercise, and it isn't. This is closer to a confession than
When the map is complete, look at it for a long time. Don't analyze it. Just look.

19.text: After you've filled in the map, which gap is the biggest? Which is the smallest? The smallest one is
where we start. Not the biggest.

20.text: I want to say this directly because it's where I lost months on my own version of this work.
You can spend a long time analyzing the map. Thinking about it. Journaling about it. Talking it through
with your friend who gets it. You can make the map more detailed. You can color-code it.
None of that moves the map.
The map gets moved by a thing you do in the life. A standing commitment cancelled. A true answer
given out loud. A drawer cleared. A Tuesday left empty because Tuesday is the day your energy
Small actions. Specific. Visible. Done by Friday.
This sounds obvious. I'm saying it anyway because the trap of this kind of work is that you can spend a
year mapping and remapping and feeling like you're doing the work. The map is not the work. The map
is the diagnostic. The work is moving one thing.
You're not going to think your way out of this. You're not going to journal your way out of it either.
You're going to do one thing.

21.text: Right now, looking at your map, what's the smallest thing you could move this week? Not the biggest.
The smallest. The one you could finish by Friday.

22.text: CHAPTER 09
The one-move method.
The protocol is small enough that your nervous system can handle it.
1. Look at your map. 2. Pick one item where the gap between LEFT and RIGHT is small. Not your
biggest misalignment. Your smallest. 3. Identify the smallest action that would close that gap by 20
percent. Not 100. Twenty. 4. Schedule it for the next 48 hours. 5. Do it. 6. Hold it. Don't change
anything else for seven days. 7. After seven days, return to the map.
Why this works. Most women try to reinvent, relocate, or burn-it-all-down their way to a life that fits.
Your body doesn't trust that. Your body knows what comes after a big move. Three weeks of
high-functioning, then a crash, then a quiet return to the old shape.
Your body trusts small. It trusts repeatable. It trusts: I'm going to move this one thing and see what
happens.
A few examples of small moves.
 Cancel the standing commitment you dread, and replace it with nothing
 Answer 'how are you' with the true answer, once, to one safe person
 Clear one shelf or drawer that belongs to a version of you that's gone
 Say no without an explanation attached. Once.
 Take back one hour on the calendar and put nothing in it
 Wear the thing you keep saving for a version of your life that never arrives
 Tell one person one true thing you've been editing out
Pick yours. Do it by Friday. Use Worksheet 4 in the back.

23.text: The move you just picked. Are you 95 percent sure you'll actually do it? If you're less than that, pick a
smaller move. The point is to keep the promise, not to be impressive.

24.text: CHAPTER 10
When “you” feels blurry.
This chapter is for when you sit down to fill in the right side of the map and you don't know what you
would do.
This is common. It doesn't mean you're broken. It means you've been so many versions for so many
people that you can't easily find the un-absorbed one. You're not lost. You're buried.
Three things help.
Look at the unperformed parts of your life.
How you'd cook a meal you actually want to eat. What you do in the first ten minutes when the house is
finally empty. How you talk to the friend you've known longest. How you'd spend a Saturday with no
one to answer to. These places hold unstyled versions of how you operate. Watch them. Notice the
patterns. Bring one back into the main life.
Strip the inputs.
For 14 days, no self-improvement content. No podcasts telling you who to become. No feeds full of
women living louder. Read fiction. Walk. Cook. By the end of 14 days, when you sit down with the area
you couldn't fill in, something usually surfaces. Your own thinking has space to come forward when
other people's thinking isn't filling the channel.
Ask a smaller question.
Instead of 'what would my life look like if it were truly me,' ask 'what's the next thing I would choose,
knowing everything I know now, if I were starting today?' The big question has too many right answers,
which is why your mind goes blank. The small one usually has one or two.

25.text: Which of the three moves above is the one you don't want to do? That's usually the one you need most.

26.text: You will slip back. Someone will need you and you'll snap into the old role before you notice. You'll hear
about another woman's routine, her renovation, her reinvention, and immediately want to install her life
on top of yours. You'll spend two days becoming her before Wednesday morning, when the dopamine
wears off, you realize it isn't yours.
This is normal. The pull to perform is stronger than the discipline to stay yourself, especially in
low-confidence weeks. You don't fix it by being harder on yourself.
1. Notice it. 'I just spent two days rearranging my life after one conversation.' 2. Stop. Don't undo
anything yet. 3. Look at your map. 4. Ask: does what I started doing close a gap on my map, or create a
new one? 5. If it creates one, set it down. It was a performance, not a move. 6. If it closes one, keep it.
The script when you catch yourself mid-slip:
I noticed I started [the thing] after [the trigger]. I'm going to wait three days. If I still want it, and it closes
a gap on my map, I'll continue. If not, I'll let it go.
No drama. No 'I'm so bad at this.' Just the protocol.

28.text: The check takes ten minutes. Do it on the same day every month.
1. What did I add to my life in the last 30 days?
2. Of those things, what looks like me?
3. What got added because someone expected it and I reacted?
4. What's one thing I want to move on the map this month?
5. What's one thing that's now actually closed?
Write the answers down. Save them somewhere you'll see them.
After three rounds of this, you'll see a pattern. The pattern is more useful than any new plan. For most
women, the pattern is one specific input. A particular person, a particular feed, a particular room they
walk into. Something that consistently pulls them out of their own life. Once you can name it, you can
decide what to do about it.

29.text: If you did this check today, what's the one thing you'd write down as having been added because
someone expected it and you reacted?

30.text: The hardest part of staying inside your own life is other people's confidence.
Someone will tell you, very surely, what you should do. Your mother. Your sister. The friend whose life
looks sorted. They will be right that it works. For someone. They will not know that it isn't you. You'll
hear the certainty in their voice and start to doubt the map.
And here's the complicated part. Some of these people are invested in the old version of you. Not
maliciously. The old you was convenient. She said yes. She held things together. When you move, their
life moves too, and some advice is really a request to move back.
1. Acknowledge it's probably good advice. For someone. 2. Note the source. Is this a person whose life
looks like yours wants to? Or someone comfortable with who you were? 3. Run it against your map.
Does adopting it close a gap or create one? 4. If it closes a gap, adopt it. 5. If it creates one, say thank
you and don't. You don't owe an explanation. You don't need to be right about why.
You will disappoint some people by declining good advice. You will gain a life that looks like you. That
is the trade. There's no version of this work that lets you say yes to everyone and still ends with your
Use Worksheet 6 in the back for advice you're not sure what to do with.

32.text: You're done with this workbook when you can ask yourself one question and answer it honestly.
If I drew my life on a piece of paper today, would it look like me?
Some of you, having done the work, can now answer yes, mostly. A few gaps remain. That's fine. You
have the protocol. You move one piece at a time. The map stays current. The check happens monthly.
You won't reach perfect alignment. That's not the goal. An aligned life isn't a life with no discomfort and
no challenges. It's a life where you know your hell yes and your hell no, and where the parts that aren't
you are parts you've chosen. Not parts you absorbed.
The standard isn't does this feel good. The standard is does this look like me on paper. The feel-good
question is too easy to manipulate. The looks-like-me question is harder to dodge. That's why we use it.
And remember what this season actually is. Life has a way of stripping us back. Heartbreak, burnout,
loss, outgrowing. Whether you wanted it or not. You're not starting over. You're starting fresh, from
You didn't lose yourself. You just left yourself out. Now you're back in.

33.text: Here's what I need to be honest about before you close this.
The map shows you what isn't yours. It's damn good at that. You now know which roles you inherited,
which commitments you absorbed, which voice you've been answering in that was never yours.
But the map has a limit. It can show you what to remove. It can't show you what was underneath the
That's not a workbook job. That's a mirror job.
Because here's what happens to some women after this work: they strip out what isn't theirs and hit a
question the map can't answer. “Okay... so who's actually left?”
If you hit that question, you're not doing it wrong. You've just reached the part that needs a second set
of eyes. Someone reading your actual blueprint, not your absorbed one, and naming the pattern you
can't see because you're standing inside it.
That's the Pre-Work Intensive. 90 minutes, 1:1. Your blueprint through Human Design and astrology.
Your pattern named. One real move that's yours by design, not by inheritance.
The workbook put you back in your life.
The Intensive shows you who “you” actually is.

43.text: You now have the map. You have the protocol. You have the standard.
The misfit doesn't fix itself. You won't journal your way out of it. You won't manifest your way out of it.
You won't read your way out of it.
You move one thing. You hold it for a week. You check the map. You move the next thing.
That's it. That's the whole work.
The life you want is the one that looks like you on paper. Not the one that feels good for an hour after a
podcast. Not the one everyone else is comfortable with.
The one that looks like you.
